items.video_title: Brake Pads Worn Out in 3 Months (or Too Fast)? Here's Why!
items.video_description:
Brake pads worn out in just 3 months? If your brake pads are wearing out too fast, there could be a hidden mechanical problem causing premature wear, even when you're not pressing the brake pedal.

In this video, we'll explain why brake pads wear out so quickly, how to recognize abnormal brake wear, and what to check before spending money on another brake replacement.

We'll cover the most common causes of premature brake pad wear, including:

- Stuck brake calipers and seized slide pins that keep pads rubbing against the rotors.
- Driving habits and excessive braking that create unnecessary friction and heat.
- Damaged or grooved brake rotors that can accelerate pad wear.
- Low-quality or unsuitable brake pads** that may not withstand your driving conditions.
- Improper brake installation and overlooked hardware problems.
- Hydraulic and parking brake faults that prevent the brakes from releasing fully.
- Corrosion, road salt, and contamination that affect brake performance and durability.

You'll also learn how to recognize uneven brake pad wear, what normal brake pad life depends on, and which warning signs could indicate a dragging brake.

10:45 Final Diagnosis: Demand, Drag, and Durability

Whether your brake pads lasted just 3 months, 5,000 miles, or considerably less than expected, this guide will help you understand the possible causes and what to discuss with your mechanic.

Don't keep replacing brake pads without finding out why they're wearing out.
